items.note: Product design education study comparing an AI-integrated instruction group with a conventional-teaching group on creativity gains; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page all failed), and search notes suggest creativity measures may be partly survey-based, with N and allocation unknown.

Experiment (described in a linked Mendeley data record as a quasi-experiment in design education) varying generative-AI assistant availability on creative problem-solving performance and academic emotions; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect 403), so N, assignment, and scoring are unconfirmed.

Randomized controlled experiment with third-year engineering students comparing ChatGPT-assisted and unassisted ideation (728 ideas) plus a survey; no significant difference in ideation outcomes, differences by prior ChatGPT experience; N of students not in abstract; distinct from the same first author's 2026 crossover study.

Two ChatGPT experiments (N = 234, 205), a Gemini replication (N = 157), and 6,290 naturalistic chats relate measured Creative Direction to originality and across-person semantic similarity; direction is measured not assigned, but the abstract mentions performance without LLM assistance, so full text must show whether AI versus no-AI conditions were assigned (possibly within-person).

Eight-week control-group design with 36 preservice Turkish teachers writing STEM stories with AI tools (19) or without tools (17); abstract says groups were 'randomly selected' (unclear whether people were randomized), stories were evaluated on textuality criteria but main outcomes are digital-literacy and 21st-century-skill scales; below 50 participants.

Process study of 14 students in dyads generating ideas with ChatGPT, coding 591 turns for cognitive strategies (most ideas repeated ChatGPT's); no comparison condition and no creativity or diversity score, though relevant background on convergence toward AI ideas.

Exploratory study in one high-school class where students wrote short stories alone or with ChatGPT 3.5, plus ChatGPT-only stories, analyzed quantitatively and qualitatively and judged by a same-age reading group; class size not stated and likely small.

Sixty reading-club members divided evenly into unassisted and Claude-assisted writers on identical horror prompts, with stories rated on originality, coherence, horror effect, character development, and impact; assignment method not stated.

One-factor between-subjects lab experiment comparing nominal, interactive, hybrid human plus GPT-3, and AI-only brainstorming groups on idea count and creativity; conference abstract (AOM Proceedings), N not in abstract (search notes say 168).

Public Halloween deployment where 832 participants generated 15,719 images in a 2x2 design varying the AI agents' emotional expressiveness and whether novelty was rewarded, measuring creative output and collective diversity; all participants use generative tools, so the contrast is AI configuration and reward design, not AI versus none, and may fail scope at full text.
